JusPrin sets OrcaSlicer's `project_load_behaviour` to load everything, so the file's printer preset is applied. On 2026-10-28 a UX walkthrough of the built app (jusprin-newui a684aee37d, Opus 5.5) rated this high; critique with screenshots at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (frames 1C-01, 1C-02, and frames 0 and 1 under Launch for the inconsistent launch path). Kenneth wants to choose between fix options before code is written: first deliverable is an untracked options note in the worktree root, then stop. Rules: fork-stewardship doc before touching OrcaSlicer-owned files, seams small and additive; `project_open`'s load report and the `file-loaded` skill are the agent's side; temp docs untracked; do not commit unless asked. Task:
Problem: opening a MakerWorld 3MF saved for a Bambu P1S changes the header printer chip to "Bambu Lab P1S · 0.4" and draws the 256 mm P1S bed, although the person owns only an A1 mini and the printer list has no P1S. Nothing in the header or canvas says the printer came from the file; only the agent's first message, about fifteen seconds later, explains "Opening the file switched your printer from the A1 mini to the P1S, but a P1S isn't one of the printers you've set up" and asks which printer to use. Anyone who slices in the meantime gets G-code for a printer they do not have, and the arrow looks like it fits because the bed drawn is the wrong one. The same conflict at launch (a resumed P1S project with the A1 mini connected) raised OrcaSlicer's "sync the printer information" dialog instead, so the two paths disagree; a separate task covers that dialog, so coordinate the decision rather than solving it twice. Frames 1C-01 and 1C-02 of the critique show both states.

Task, in this order:
1. Reproduce in the real app (recipe in the background notes). Trace the open path: `ShellController::take_opened_files`, `Plater::load_project`, the `project_load_behaviour` setting, and where the fake printer's connection does or does not trigger OrcaSlicer's sync question. Record what the file's embedded printer does to the preset bundle (is a P1S system preset installed on the fly, or a project-embedded preset) and what the header chip and plate drawing read.
2. Write an untracked options note (`file-printer-switch-options.md` in the worktree root) with two to four options, each with what the person sees in the first second, the OrcaSlicer-owned lines touched and their rebase cost, how it interacts with the agent's first message and `project_open`'s load report, and a recommendation. Candidates: keep the person's selected printer and import only the file's process and filament settings, with the agent told what the file wanted; apply the file's printer but mark the header chip "from the file" until the person or the agent confirms a printer; apply it and have the plate drawing and chip show the mismatch the way the product definition's "compact printer pointer and any mismatch" describes.
3. Stop and wait for Kenneth to choose. Do not implement before he answers.

Done, after his choice, means: within a second of opening a file for another printer, the header makes the situation visible without a modal; launch and open behave the same way; verified in the real app with screenshots; backward compatibility of 3MF loading kept and any OrcaSlicer-owned change recorded as fork-stewardship requires.

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachn

... [1516 characters truncated] ...

kward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.

- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.
# JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-newui`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
8. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, execution and verification requirements.
9. [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md) — managed project storage, migration, restore, export, retention, and failure behavior.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Print-host (Klipper/Moonraker) simulation stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`.

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

## Source lineage

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.

# Fork stewardship

**Status:** Required discipline for every change to an upstream-owned file on `jusprin-newui`.

JusPrin is a long-lived fork. Every line it changes in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line it re-resolves at every rebase, forever, by a person who was not there when the line was written. The rules below exist to keep that permanent cost small and, where it cannot be small, to keep it visible.

One question generates all of them: **after this change, what does the fork own?**

- Owning *product policy* is safe. It is ours, upstream will never write it, and it lives in our files.
- Owning a *small neutral seam* is acceptable. It is the kind of thing upstream might plausibly have written itself, so it survives refactors and could be contributed back.
- Owning *upstream's behavior* is the expensive kind. It commits us to re-deriving upstream's intent forever, and the day we take ownership is usually the day the behavior quietly diverges.

Two mechanical facts drive everything else. Git merges text, not meaning: it conflicts when two sides touch the same or adjacent lines, and it stays silent when they touch different lines even if the result is nonsense. And a conflict is a *stop* — a human is forced to look — while silent divergence is unbounded and invisible. Conflicts are therefore not the enemy. Unnoticed drift is, and conflicts that resolve wrongly are.

## The ten principles

### 1. Conflict probability is about where you write, not how much

**Rule.** Place fork edits where upstream rarely writes, and keep the number of distinct sites low.

**Mechanism.** Risk is roughly *how often upstream edits this region* times *how much of the region you occupy*, summed over every place you touched. Each site is an independent draw. New files have probability zero, so their size is free; one line inside a function upstream is actively reworking is expensive.

**The test.** How many separate places does this change touch, and how busy is each one? Would one seam deliver the same capability?

**Violation.** Delivering a single capability through a dozen scattered notification lines across several upstream files, when one funnel that every path already passes through would have carried them.

### 2. A clean merge is not a safe merge

**Rule.** Prefer edits that are locally correct over edits that participate in upstream's control flow.

**Mechanism.** Git merges text. If your edit's correctness depends on the code around it — an ordering, a guard, an early return, an invariant nobody wrote down — upstream can restructure the surroundings, the merge succeeds, and your edit now runs under assumptions that no longer hold, with no signal at all.

**The test.** If upstream restructures the code around this hunk, do I get a conflict or silence? If silence, would any test catch it?

**Violation.** Moving a member out of a constructor's initializer list because a callback can fire mid-construction. Nothing in upstream's code records that invariant, so a future cleanup restores the old form with no conflict and no error.

### 3. Add to upstream's code; do not revise it

**Rule.** Append, insert, and call. Do not rewrite upstream functions or change their signatures.

**Mechanism.** An additive hook fails gracefully: when it conflicts, the resolution is "keep both," and anyone can do that correctly. A rewritten function fails badly: every future upstream change to it is a conflict whose resolution requires re-deriving two intents at once, in code no longer shared with upstream. Rewriting subtle logic also tends to change it, and you find out later.

**The test.** Does upstream's line survive my change? If I deleted or replaced one, why could I not have added next to it?

**Violation.** Replacing OrcaSlicer's undo and redo implementations with fork-owned equivalents in order to learn whether the history position moved. Re-expressing the vendor-specific snapshot walk silently dropped one of its branches. An additive helper that reports the result, leaving upstream's functions untouched, would have answered the same question.

### 4. Own the policy; borrow the mechanism

**Rule.** No product name, color, dimension, or product-specific decision in an upstream-owned file. Upstream files may gain small neutral capabilities; the policy that uses them lives in fork-owned code.

**Mechanism.** Product specifics in upstream files are permanent divergence: they can never be upstreamed and never dropped, so they must be re-resolved forever. A neutral capability — a flag, a getter/setter pair, an event — reads like something upstream could have written, which is exactly why it survives refactors.

**The test.** Would this addition look reasonable in an upstream pull request, with no explanation of our product?

**Violation.** A product-named enum value inside a rendering class, or product decisions embedded in an upstream mouse handler. The fix is a neutral options struct plus a fork-owned controller that applies o

nd CI files that JusPrin has never edited.

## Before you finish

A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:

1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against current upstream and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.

   ```bash
   git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<fork base> upstream/main HEAD
   ```

   For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy one is a defect to fix now, not a note for later.

2. **An account of every upstream line deleted or rewritten.** Where the logic went, and why an additive form was not possible.

3. **A statement of what the fork now owns.** Policy, a neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.

An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.

## This fork's terrain

Facts specific to OrcaSlicer, worth knowing before choosing where to put a seam. They change over time; re-measure rather than trusting these.

`Plater.cpp` is by far the busiest file the fork touches, followed by the central `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt`, `GLCanvas3D.cpp`, and `PartPlate.cpp`. `GLToolbar` and `GLGizmosManager` are quiet. File-level churn is only a first approximation: some functions inside `Plater.cpp` have not been touched upstream in the entire life of this fork, and a seam there is far cheaper than the file's overall rate suggests. Measure the function, not just the file.

Some native state is shared rather than owned by one object. OrcaSlicer's collapse toolbar belongs to `Plater` and is used by both the Prepare and Preview canvases, so a per-canvas guard cannot save and restore it correctly. Shared state needs one owner at the shared lifetime boundary, and exact restoration needs a getter as well as a setter.

`MainFrame`'s Notebook is cheaper to wrap than to dismantle. Dozens of
upstream predicates — menu and shortcut enabling, `can_delete`, slice status
updates, undo/redo gating — key off `m_tabpanel->GetSelection()`, so removing
or reparenting the Prepare/Preview pages breaks them with no conflict and no
error. A shell gets a tabless full-window layout for free instead: hide the
strip via the public `GetBtnsListCtrl()` (wxBookCtrlBase gives a hidden
controller zero size, so pages fill the client area), and the stock slice and
print side buttons disappear with it because `ButtonsListCtrl` reparents them
into the strip at construction. The Phase 1 production shell reached a
19-added-line upstream footprint this way where the POC's reparenting shell
needed edits across eight upstream files.

The same measurement gives the rule for every fork-owned screen that comes
after the shell. OrcaSlicer's surfaces (the stock homepage, Prepare, Preview,
Monitor, the settings tabs) stay inside the Notebook, because their
correctness depends on it. Fork-owned surfaces (the header, the Agent pane,
Home, and whatever follows) live outside it, as siblings of the Notebook in a
fork-owned sizer, shown and hidden by the shell. The shell *reads* the
Notebook's selection to decide what to show and *never edits its page list*:
no `RemovePage`, `InsertPage`, or reparenting of a stock page. Removing or
replacing a page hands the fork the meaning of that index. Upstream keeps
addressing it by number — `tpHome` as a dialog parent, the target of
`EVT_LOAD_URL`, the tab `post_init` returns to — and every one of those lands
on the fork's widget with no conflict and no error. If a fork surface truly
must be a page, append it last, where no upstream code addresses it.

Navigation between screens stays a Notebook selection change even when the
screen being left is fork-owned. Menu and shortcut enabling, undo and redo
availability, and slice-status updates all read `GetSelection()`, so the
selection must remain the one record of which OrcaSlicer surface is active.
Showing Prepare any other way leaves those predicates answering for the wrong
page, silently.

Some stock behavior is already exposed as an event idiom rather than a
function. Upstream itself drives plate slicing from two places with the same
sequence — the slice button and the Cmd+R shortcut both run
`plater->update(true, true)`, post `EVT_GLTOOLBAR_SLICE_PLATE` to the Plater,
and select the Preview tab — so fork code may repeat that short dispatch
without violating the shared-implementation rule; the behavior itself stays
owned by Plater's event handler.

Historical measurements and the incidents behind several of these rules are in the [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) and, for the spike era, in the [POC reference](poc-reference.md).

# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)

Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.

The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
fake unless asked.

This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.

## What success looks like

- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.

## Turn it on

Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.

Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
`orca`.

**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.

Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
config. JusPrin turns `single_instance` on at every start; its instance lock
lives in the data directory, so a scratch `--datadir` runs as its own instance
beside another JusPrin. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

For an MCP client, the shell harness does all of this in its own datadir:
`shell_integration_harness --manual-mcp <dir> --fake-printer` saves a
**Fake A1 mini** printer, connects it to the fake and selects it before it
prints `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY`. Edits to the conf would not survive: the
fixture rewrites it at startup.

## Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
fake rereads it about once a second.

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |

No `spools` (or an empty array) reports no AMS at all, same as before this
field existed. A non-empty array reports one AMS unit (id `"0"`) with one
tray per spool, up to 4:

```json
{"spools": [{"subBrands": "PLA Matte", "trayType": "PLA", "colour": "5F7D4FFF"}]}
```

`subBrands` is what `PrinterDiscovery.cpp` reads back as the spool's name
when set (ahead of `trayType`), so it is the field worth setting for a
saved/network-printer card or receipt to show something. `trayType` is the
spool's material (Home's Loaded row names it); the fake sends it beside a
`tray_info_idx`, since upstream ignores a type that arrives without one.
`filamentId` sets that id (`"GFA01"` is Bambu PLA Matte); left out, the
id is empty, and Orca's filament sync skips the tray. `colour` is optional: a spool without it reports no colour, and Home
draws no swatch for it.

Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.

## Print

Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.

If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
scenario after send.

## Isolate a running app (agents)

Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.

On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.

Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events
posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer

### Opening and importing files

Decided 2026-10-24. A file reaches JusPrin in a handful of ways, and they mean one of two things: **start from this file**, or **add this to the project I am working on**. The first is what a person means almost every time they bring a file in; the second is the minority case (a multi-part print), and the person signals it by aiming at the plate or by asking the agent. Because autosave keeps every project, starting a new project by mistake costs one click on Recent, while adding to the wrong project leaves a stray part in it. So every way in starts a new project unless the person aimed at the plate.

| How the file is opened | Model file (STL, STEP, OBJ, AMF, …) | .3mf |
|---|---|---|
| Opened from the OS: a double-click in Finder or Explorer, "Open with", a browser's "open in JusPrin" | New project, named after the file; the app goes to Prepare | New project; the "Previously opened file" question if the file was opened before |
| Dropped on Home | Same | Same |
| Home's **Open…** button, File › Open Project (Cmd+O) | Same | Same |
| Dropped on the Prepare canvas | Added to the open project | New project, as above. OrcaSlicer's "open as project or import geometry?" question is not asked |
| **+ Add model** in the Plates and Project pane, File › Import (Cmd+I) | Added to the open project | Its geometry is added to the open project, without its settings (OrcaSlicer's Import) |
| The Agent composer's + › 3D model, a drop on the Agent pane, or a request in the chat | Attached; the agent adds it to the open project (`object_import`) | Same |

Rules that follow from the table:

- A model file never silently lands in whatever project happened to be open behind Home. Before 2026-10-24 Home's Import button did exactly that, because it called OrcaSlicer's `add_model`, and from 2026-09-30 a project was always open behind Home (the most recent one resumes at startup).
- A file opened from the OS lands in the running JusPrin. OrcaSlicer's default starts a second process for a .3mf; JusPrin runs as a single instance on every platform.
- Several files opened or dropped together make one new project holding all of them.
- Opening a .3mf as a project is the only thing a .3mf does on the Prepare canvas. Wanting only the geometry out of a .3mf is rare, and the agent or File › Import can do it on request. The one question JusPrin asks on a file open stays the "Previously opened file" question described in the [autosave document](autosave-version-history.md).
- Home's primary action is **Open…**, not Import: there is nothing on Home to import into. The whole Home page accepts a dropped file, and its empty state says so ("Drop a model or project here, or Open…"). Beside it, **New** is the design system's compact outlined button (`secondarySmall`, 28 DIP) for a blank project built up part by part, quiet enough not to compete with Open; File › New Project does the same.
- G-code files keep OrcaSlicer's behavior (the G-code viewer) for now.
- In the chat, a load that started a new project draws one quiet line, "Opened bracket.3mf as a new project · you · 10:42" (the page's `MessageList`, from the file report's `projectOpened`); an import into the open project draws nothing, since the timeline's step rows already say what was added. With no agent the same report draws the "Notes about this file" card instead.

**Finding the way to add a part.** With Home's button named Open, the person who wants a second part in the project they have needs to find it from Prepare. Every slicer solves this the same way, with a control inside the workspace that is always on screen: PrusaSlicer's Add button on the top toolbar and Cmd+I, Cura's folder icon at the top left of Prepare, and OrcaSlicer's own Add button on the main toolbar, which JusPrin hides. Dragging onto the plate is in addition to that control in all three, never the only way. JusPrin keeps the same shape: a **+ Add model** button under the plate list in the Plates tab of the Plates and Project pane, drawn like **+ Add plate** and placed directly above it, so the two things that can be added there sit together with the commoner one first (chosen on 2026-10-24 from a drawn comparison against a plus in the tab header and a row under the open plate), plus File › Import (Cmd+I), the composer's + menu, and the empty plate's hint ("Drop a model here or add one"). A person who asks the agent to add a file gets it added as well.

Ownership: the policy is fork-owned (the Home backend, the shell's file handler and the Prepare canvas's drop target, the Plates pane's button). OrcaSlicer keeps its file dialogs, its loading code and its "Previously opened file" seam; the fork adds one seam, `Plater::set_external_file_open_handler`, that lets it take the files handed to `Plater::load_files(wxArrayString)` (the OS, another instance, the command line, a download, a drop) before OrcaSlicer adds them to the open project, and sets two of OrcaSlicer's own settings (`single_instance`, `project_load_behaviour`) to the values the table needs.

How the paths come out of that one seam:

- The shell's handler (`ShellController::take_opened_files`) leaves a .3mf to OrcaSlicer, which opens it as a project through `load_project` and so asks the "Previously opened file" question; files given with it are added to that project. Any other files are opened in a new project named after the first one: the open project is saved and released the way the agent's `project_open` releases it, then OrcaSlicer's own load runs into the new project, and the app goes to Prepare.
- A drop on the Prepare canvas must add, so the shell replaces OrcaSlicer's `PlaterDropTarget` with its own, which loads through the same call while telling the handler to stand aside. OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own target after every slice; the shell puts its own back on the next idle turn. OrcaSlicer's one-SVG emboss on drop is not kept (the shell hides that gizmo); a dropped SVG loads as an object.
- File › Import › Import Zip Archive also reaches `load_files(wxArrayString)`, so a zip on its own keeps OrcaSlicer's behavior and adds. Home's Open… and a drop on Home open a zip in a new project like any model file.
- A file dropped on Home reaches the app as its name and bytes, not its path: the web view takes the drop. On macOS a native drop target on the web view would not see it: wxWidgets 3.3 gives its WebKit view none of the drag methods it gives its own views, so WebKit's own handling runs (read from the wxWidgets source on 2026-10-24; not yet tried with a real drag). The bytes are written to `JusPrin-dropped/<MD5>/<name>` under the system temp folder and opened from there, so the "Previously opened file" question recognizes a .3mf dropped on Home before, but not one first opened from its own folder.
- The agent's tools load through the vector overload of `load_files` and `load_project`, which the seam does not see, and the handler stands aside while a tool's load runs.

### Print issues and OrcaSlicer's notifications

Inside the shell OrcaSlicer's own notifications are held but not drawn. JusPrin reads the list back and draws what it holds: print problems as a status pill in the canvas's lower right corner, the list it opens, and a bubble beside the object the selected issue is about, with **Ask AI** and **Resolve with AI**; the outcome of an action (export finished, an arrange that was refused) as a short confirmation above the pill; and work that is still running (a slice, an arrange, an export) as an entry in the chat.

**OrcaSlicer's notification list is the source of truth.** A notification carries a kind, a level and words. It does not carry the object it is about, so where OrcaSlicer lets its check be asked again, that check is asked once more for the object only.

| Piece | Owns |
|---|---|
| `PrintIssues/NoticeKinds` | Where each of OrcaSlicer's notification kinds goes: the issue list, a confirmation, running work, application state, or nowhere. Every kind is named; a kind OrcaSlicer adds stops the build in this file until someone routes it. |
| `PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor` | Reads the list on the notification manager's own turn, compares it with what it saw last, and rebuilds only on a change. Asks OrcaSlicer's checks for the object behind a validation, a copy over the plate's edge, an object out of a nozzle's reach and a slicing step warning. Holds no rule about what a problem is. |
| `issues_from` in `PrintIssues/PrintIssue` | The rule, as plain data with its own tests: an object lookup's entry exists only while OrcaSlicer holds a notification of its kind; a print-problem notification no lookup answers for is a plate-wide issue in OrcaSlicer's words. |
| `PrintIssues/IssueOverlayLayout`, `IssueOverlay` | Where the pieces go, how they are drawn and how they close, with ImGui inside the canvas's frame through the same overlay hook as the tool strip. The bubble never covers its object, the pill, a confirmation or the tool strip. |
| `PrintIssues/WorkFeed` | Work as it starts, moves on and ends. A slice is followed through OrcaSlicer's own events, which carry a percentage and an outcome. Other work is read from the "still running" notifications, which carry neither. |
| `AgentHost::begin_work`, `update_work`, `finish_work`; `WorkCard` in the page | The entry in the chat: saved with the project at the place in the timeline where the work started, so a later message reads below it; a progress bar and, where the work can be stopped, Cancel while it runs; completed in place. The chat panel opens when work starts. Repeats are folded by the page, never in what is saved, and an entry still "running" in a project that was closed mid-run reads as interrupted. |
| `PrintIssues/IssueContext`, `AgentHost::submit_issue_message` | The chat message a button sends, and the one way a message enters the chat from outside the page. |

Two things are read whether or not a notification exists, because OrcaSlicer's notifications do not cover them in time:

- **The slice result.** A path outside the plate, a filament its nozzle cannot reach, and a filament that cannot print on the plate surface get their notifications only when OrcaSlicer's preview loads the slice, which here means opening Check print. OrcaSlicer refuses to print from the moment the slice ends.
- **Why a slice failed.** A critical failure is shown in a dialog and leaves no notification, and no notification says which object the failure named. `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` is the only place both exist.

Rules that follow:

- **No pill is the all-clear, and it is never given before a check.** The pill is drawn only while OrcaSlicer reports an issue, ignored ones included. While OrcaSlicer holds an unapplied edit the last issues are kept, the pill says it is checking and both buttons are off, so the pill does not go until OrcaSlicer has looked. An issue that was not in the list before is announced once by a ring that spreads from the pill twice; an edit that keeps an issue, and ignoring one or undoing that, announce nothing.
- **Nothing is resolved by the fork.** An issue goes when OrcaSlicer lets go of its notification. An agent saying it fixed something changes nothing.
- **"Blocks printing" is OrcaSlicer's answer.** An error-level notification blocks. For the slice result it is OrcaSlicer's own post-slice check, which allows a path 2 mm past the plate edge; the monitor does not apply a stricter test of its own.
- **The object is never read out of the words.** Two messages of one kind are told apart by comparing OrcaSlicer's words now with its words before, as OrcaSlicer does itself. Which object a message is about always comes from a check's own ids.
- **A press acts on what is true at the press**, and with no assistant set up it sends nothing and offers the chat panel's setup. **The two buttons differ only in the sentence**: Ask AI and Resolve with AI send the same context and the turn gets the same tools.
- **Operation failures are not print issues.** A failed download or a refused arrange is a confirmation, never an entry in the issue list.
- **Closing hides, it never resolves.** The pill is always there and is the way back; the list and the bubble are opened and closed, one at a time, and closing either changes nothing about the issue or the count. The list closes on a pick, a second press of the pill, Escape, or a press outside it. The bubble belongs to the selection: opening it selects its object, and it closes when that object stops being selected, which is what a click on the empty plate, Escape and a click on another object already do in OrcaSlicer. Turning the view or dragging the object leaves it open. Its close button leaves the selection alone, and a press on **Ask AI** or **Resolve with AI** that reaches the chat closes it. With one issue the pill opens the bubble directly, and with several the bubble's pager walks them all. The overlay hears Escape and presses through handlers of its own on the canvas's window, bound after OrcaSlicer's and so called first; no OrcaSlicer file is involved.
- **Ignoring a warning is the person's mark, not OrcaSlicer's.** **Ignore this warning** in the bubble leaves OrcaSlicer's notification alone: the warning stays in the list, marked, below the ones that count, and the pill stops counting it ("1 warning ignored" when nothing else is left, never "No print issues"). Only a warning can be ignored; a blocker cannot, because OrcaSlicer would still refuse to print. An ignore lasts while OrcaSlicer keeps reporting that warning on the active plate's own list, and is forgotten when OrcaSlicer stops, so a warning that comes back is shown again. It is not saved with the project. The rule is `mark_ignored` in `PrintIssues/PrintIssue`.

Known limits: application and account notifications (update available, plug-in missing, preset sync conflict) are routed to `App` and drawn nowhere yet. A confirmation shows OrcaSlicer's words and a close button; the actions OrcaSlicer attached to its own notification (open folder, eject, cancel an upload) are not offered. Only a slice has a percentage and a known ending; other work shows a bar with no amount and is recorded as done unless its Cancel was pressed. Uploads and downloads have not been run. The tips and the object size card are not shown.

### Agent WebView

The production Agent interface is a separate React/TypeScript package that runs locally inside a `wxWebView`. It needs:

- a versioned schema for commands and events;
- scripted mock conversations that play back the same way every time, for UI tests;
- messages that render as they stream in, with a scroll position that does not jump;
- written rules for keyboard, focus, shortcuts, clipboard, text selection, and IME (the input method used to type languages such as Chinese and Japanese);
- a defined state for each of these: reloading, starting up, an error in the bridge between the page and the app, and the agent being unavailable;
- no project state of its own. OrcaSlicer's project state stays in C++.

---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. metadata:

Lessons from driving the printer chat through `--printer-live` with the live model and the fake Bambu printer:

- **A reply's later lines have no `HARNESS LIVE` prefix.** A `Choices:` line sits on its own log line, so `grep "HARNESS LIVE"` hides it. On 2026-09-23 this produced a wrong report that the model never offered choices. Grep `^Choices:` separately.
- **A failed run keeps its data dir, with the API key in it.** The harness prints `HARNESS DATA DIR kept for inspection: /var/folders/.../jusprin-shell-*`. Delete the dir your own run printed, by that path. Do not sweep every `jusprin-shell-*` holding a key: another session may be running the harness in the same checkout, and on 2026-09-23 a sweep deleted a live instance's data dir.
- **Re-selecting the selected Bambu LAN printer deselects it.** DevManager's "same lan machine" path disconnects and reconnects, and GUI_App's local-connect handler (CallAfter) then sees the lost status and calls `set_selected_machine("")` after the reconnect. The connection reports "The selected printer changed". `OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_printer` now deselects and re-selects on the next event turn. The fake printer auto-selects itself when discovered, so the first connect always hits this.
- **Close OrcaSlicer's printer list (GuideFrame) only after its page loads.** It installs its web page's script handler from a CallAfter that waits on the page; `EndModal` before the load leaves that wait hanging on a hidden view, and the app freezes with no window. On 2026-09-23 this was first blamed on the product and "fixed" with a deferral, then traced to the test and reverted. Wait for `!is_adding_script_handler()`, a non-busy page and a URL, as the old `setup_manual` check did.
- **Open the panel through `ShellController::open_printer_conversation`** in live tests; `PrinterPanel::open` skips the full-window layout.
- **The model's reliability is measured, not assumed.** gpt-5.4-mini saved changes without waiting for yes in 6 of 10 runs, even with an explicit "ask, then stop" prompt. Count across several runs before calling prompt wording fixed.

See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]].

**2026-10-21, opens ignored since 2026-09-29:** `ShellController::open_printer_conversation` returns without opening while a task chat is open (guard from bb29582ff7), and `PrinterPanel::close` finishes in a CallAfter that clears that flag. The live script (written 2026-09-18) opened new chats while one was open or straight after a close, so those opens were silently ignored: the "Change" session kept the earlier Add thread, and a reopen right after a close was torn down by the late close (`--printer-live` 15 failures). Fixed in the add-printer-popup worktree (uncommitted): `live_show` closes an open chat and queues the open with CallAfter, and every "open:" step waits for `IsShown()`. `--printer-setup` gained `verify_printer_chat_reopens_fresh` (close, wait for Home, reopen, thread empty). Not a product bug: Home only returns after the close finishes.
**Queue order trap (2026-10-21):** PrinterPanel::close finishes via the panel's own CallAfter; an open queued with wxGetApp().CallAfter can run first (separate queues, no order) and is refused. Queue with live_panel()->CallAfter.

---
name: file-loaded
trigger: file_loaded
---

# The first message after a file is opened or imported

The rules above still apply. For this one response, write the first message about the file just opened or imported, by the person or by a tool call of mine. Report and offer from the report and the picture, and change nothing the person has not asked for.

The report separates four sources. The app-computed opening outcome (loadFacts, loads, and objects) establishes what was loaded and how the selected printer, material and print settings changed. A load's withSettings only says the app requested settings, not that it applied them; claim they were applied only when loadFacts.settingsOutcome says applied. If that outcome is absent, leave the application of settings uncertain. The current workspace establishes what is selected now; setupPrinters lists printer models the person has set up in JusPrin, each with bedMm, its bed's width, depth and printable height; selectedPrinterBedMm is the selected printer's. For each object, placedOnBed says whether it sits wholly on the bed now, clear of any area the printer's profile excludes, and fitsSelectedBed and fitsSetupPrinters whether its size fits each bed somewhere, turned a quarter-turn if needed: an object that is off the bed but fits it needs moving, not resizing. mesh is the app's check of the model: shells is how many separate pieces it is made of, openEdges or repairedErrors above zero mean holes or errors in it, and unitsSuspicion says when its size looks like inches or metres. customized lists what the file already prepared for printing: painted supports, seams, colours or fuzzy skin, and its own layer heights. fileFacts is what each 3MF says about itself: the app that saved it, the printer and nozzle it was made for, and its filaments. Neither a selection nor that list proves which physical machine they intend to use. The raw messages.items contain Orca's dialog title and text, offered buttons, and the answer JusPrin supplied automatically. The person did not choose that answer and may never have seen the dialog. The file's details.description and details.profileDescription are author notes: claims from the file, not proof that their advice was applied. The picture, when present, is the active plate after the load, rendered from the iso view.

Look at the attached picture when there is one. Check the selected printer, filament and process presets and the plate type against the file and against the printers the person has set up; when one looks wrong for this print, say which and suggest the one to use, without changing it. When an object does not fit the selected printer, name a set-up printer it fits, from fitsSetupPrinters.

Write about 80 words, with at most two bullets, about what matters for this file now. The person sees the setup card above your message, with the presets, the plate and the estimates, and the activity line under your turn, with the checks you made: leave those to them rather than restating them.
- Lead with what decides whether or how it can print: a load that failed, an object that does not fit, a printer to choose, settings or G-code that need review. Say it once, with only the numbers that matter.
- Say what you take the object to be, and how it should be printed, only when that changes the advice, and then briefly, as a guess. Leave other advice (material, strength, orientation) until the main decision is made.
- Do not explain routine loading: how the file was opened, whether its settings were applied, or which notices appeared, unless it changes the next step. Do not imply that loading the file ran G-code on a printer. Never claim a warning was fixed merely because its dialog was dismissed.
- When nothing needs attention, say so in a sentence.
- End with exactly one question, about the next step: the message's only question, not a menu of alternatives. Do not offer to print while the intended printer or another consequential choice is unresolved.

Read each actual notice with its automatic answer and the final opening outcome. The guide below is deliberately not a code classification table.

| Notice or event you may encounter | Importance and explanation for the person |
| --- | --- |
| A newer or partly incompatible 3MF asks whether to continue | If opening succeeded, mention a lost or changed feature only when the outcome shows one. If it failed, explain the failure. Omit a version warning with no consequence. |
| Settings were substituted with supported values | Usually omit when completed successfully. Explain briefly if the result materially changes the print or still needs a choice. |
| “Customized Preset” or a file setting has no installed match | This alone does not establish that machine commands changed. Use the final selected printer and material to judge the consequence. |
| “Modified G-code” | When the notice says so, the file includes modified G-code in its printer or filament settings, and I warned about it while opening the file. G-code is the instructions a printer runs. Name the affected setting if the notice gives it and that helps locate what to review; do not invent a line number or claim I inspected the commands. Explain that these instructions need review before printing, without claiming they are safe or unsafe. Offer to review the modified G-code next. |
| Invalid values in a 3MF | If the model loaded, say which file settings need checking when their names are supplied. Do not say they were corrected unless the outcome establishes that. |
| Zero-volume parts were removed | Mention omitted parts when they could change the intended model. If nothing usable remains, lead with the failed opening. |
| “Object too small” asks whether to scale | The recorded answer says whether JusPrin scaled it. If it stayed tiny, state its final numeric size and ask the intended size. If scaled, mention the conversion only if it matters. |
| “Object too large” asks whether to shrink | The answer and final dimensions say whether it was shrunk. If still too large, explain the bed-fit problem. If shrunk, explain that its intended size may have changed. |
| A choice to open a 3MF as a project or geometry only | Use loadFacts.settingsOutcome to say whether the file's print settings were applied. Explain only when it changes the next step. |
| Connected-printer synchronization | Use the final selection and separately supplied connection state. Do not infer a connected machine from a preset name. |
| OBJ colour mapping, STEP mesh options, or unreadable STEP names | Mention a resulting colour, shape, precision or naming problem only when it matters to this model. |
| Multiple parts or files become one object | Mention grouping only if it changes how the person can print or edit the model. |
| A suggestion to simplify a very detailed model | Usually omit from the first message unless a current performance or editing problem exists. |
| A refusal to mix G-code with models, open multiple G-code files, or add models in preview mode | If the requested file did not open, explain that directly and give the next useful step. |
| “File contains no geometry” or a loading error | Lead with what failed and what, if anything, was added. Give the actual reason when available; do not invent one. |

An alarming notice does not override the final outcome. An automatic “No”, “Yes” or “OK” is JusPrin's action, not the person's preference. If several issues matter, address the most important decision first and briefly flag another consequential issue for later. If selectedSetupChange.printerPreset exists, name both its from and to selections in plain language, then ask which printer the person intends to use. Do not turn an already completed change into a fresh action item.

Use useful file author advice only when it affects the next step; keep it secondary to an unresolved printer or size decision. Attribute it to the file.

When the workspace's plan needs reassessment (its validity is needs_reassessment because the person imported this file into a project that already had a plan), record the plan again with setup_record in this reply: a new headline if the file changes how you will print, the same headline if the plan still holds. That clears the mark on the setup card; nothing else does.

Write in uiLanguage when it is supplied. Keep it short.

`jusprin-newui` (the current working branch as of 2026-09-16) carries an in-process fake Bambu printer, landed as two commits: `7acf075aaa` (implementation, 2026-09-08 10:57) and `e04c0d40d3` (docs, 2026-09-08 11:00). Operator guide: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.

**Design:** unlike the Moonraker simulator ([[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]], which fakes the wire protocol and lives on a different branch entirely), this keeps a real Bambu Lab **system** preset selected (so `PresetBundle::is_bbl_vendor()` stays true and every Bambu-only UI gate passes) and substitutes only the printer-agent implementation, at the `NetworkAgentFactory` factory level, under id `jusprin-fake-bambu`. Two earlier attempts (`a162493544`, `3c244108b4`, both reverted same day) tried faking a *non-Bambu* agent or patching the header chip directly — both failed because Bambu-only gates rejected them or because it only patched a symptom. Faking Bambu's real network (MQTT/TLS 8883, FTPS 990, discovery) was evaluated and explicitly rejected as out of scope.

**The seam:** exactly 4 added lines in `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:3574-3579`, 1 include + 3 body lines) — inside the existing `if (preset_bundle->is_bbl_vendor())` branch, `fake_bambu_printer_agent_id(app_config)` overrides `effective_agent_id` when fake mode is on, otherwise the branch is untouched. No upstream line deleted.

**Config surface is a JSON file only, no MCP tools** (Kenneth's explicit call): turn it on via `"jusprin": {"fake_printer": true}` in `JusPrin2.conf` (JSON booleans store as the string `"true"`; an INI `[jusprin]` block is silently ignored), then drive live state by writing `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (reread ~1s) with `state`/`progress`/`nozzle`/`bed`/`offline` keys. The C++ parameter carrying the datadir into the agent is misleadingly named `log_dir` (an upstream `NetworkAgentFactory::PrinterAgentFactory` convention, documented as "Directory for log files") — verified it's actually `data_dir()` at the call site, not a log subdirectory; don't be misled by the name when reading the code.

Emulates printer type `N1` (`JUSPRIN_FAKE_BAMBU_PRINTER_TYPE`), device id `FAKE001`, shows as **JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)** in Select Machine. Idle/Printing/Offline is the printer-menu **first row** (opened by clicking the printer half of the chip), never on the chip itself. The heartbeat thread does not start in the constructor — only in `set_queue_on_main_fn` when a real callback is set — so unit tests that never wire that callback stay quiet. Test target: `jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (`tests/jusprin/test_fake_bambu_agent.cpp`), coexists with `shell_theme_tests` in the same CMakeLists (their merge was a conflict the cherry-pick resolved by keeping both).

3:// Named printers: one machine a person owns, with a name they chose.

5:// OrcaSlicer has no printer object. Its "Physical Printer" dialog saves the
6:// connection settings into a user printer profile under a name the person
7:// types, and the collection that once held physical printers is never loaded.
8:// So a named printer here *is* an Orca user printer profile: the profile name
9:// is the printer's name, two machines of the same model are two profiles that
10:// inherit the same system profile, and everything Orca does with profiles --
11:// the settings tab, the sidebar combo, cloud sync -- keeps working unchanged.

# Opening a 3MF saved for another printer: options

Untracked working note, 2026-10-28, worktree `fervent-goldstine-fb2636` (branch cut from `jusprin-newui` a684aee37d). Critique frames 1C-01, 1C-02 and Launch 0 and 1 in https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR. No code changed.

## The problem, reproduced

Setup: scratch copy of the built app (`build/arm64`, binary of 2026-10-27 10:06) with its own data directory, in-process fake Bambu A1 mini connected, named printer "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2" selected, no agent key (so no model turn ran), file `find_my_hollow.3mf` (MakerWorld, saved by Bambu Studio for a P1S, three PLA colours, 233 mm arrow).

Opening the file (through the OS-open path, which lands in the same `Plater::load_files(wxArrayString)` call Home's Open… uses; the desktop-control request was declined so I could not click the button itself):

| Time after the open | What the app did (log) |
|---|---|
| +0.0 s | `load_files` → `load_project` |
| +0.84 s | `load_external_preset: change preset Bambu Lab P1S 0.4 nozzle 's value to find_my_hollow.3mf 's values`, then `select_preset: machine set Bambu Lab P1S 0.4 nozzle, idx 58 to visible` and `machine select success … is_system 1` |
| +1.03 s | `reset_size: before 180×180×180, after 256×256×250` (the plate is redrawn as the P1S bed) |
| +2.0 s | OrcaSlicer's "Tips" dialog ("Connected printer is Bambu Lab A1 mini … sync the printer information and automatically switch the preset?") is answered **No** by JusPrin, unseen |

The workspace one second after the open: `printerPreset: "Bambu Lab P1S 0.4 nozzle"`, `filamentPreset: "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL P1S 0.4 nozzle(find_my_hollow.3mf)"`. The preset list shows the P1S as a **system** preset, selected, where before the open it was hidden (P1S is not in the config's `models` list and never becomes a named printer; Home's printer column still lists only the six named printers plus the fake). The header chip reads "Bambu Lab P1S · 0.4" because the chip shows a named printer's name, or otherwise the preset's `printer_model` (`SetupCommands::current_printer`). The "Notes about this file" card (what the chat shows with no agent) lists the Tips question with "JusPrin answered No to this question."

So: the file's printer is not a project-embedded preset. OrcaSlicer finds the real P1S system profile by name, applies the file's values on top of it as a dirty edit, selects it and makes it visible. The bed, the chip, the filament list and every slice follow it.

At launch with that project resumed and the same fake printer connected, the same Tips dialog is shown to the person as a modal over "Loading…" (reproduced; the main window title was still "Loading..."). Answering Yes runs OrcaSlicer's `select_preset` on the dirty P1S preset, which is the "Transfer or discard changes" dialog of frame 1.

## Why the two paths differ

Both paths run the same `Plater::load_files` with `LoadConfig`, including the connected-printer check at its end. The difference is one fork seam:

- Home's Open…, a Finder open, a drop and the command line all enter `load_files(wxArrayString)` and `load_project`, each wrapped in the fork's `FileOpenScope` (Plater.cpp lines 12145 and 14216). `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::file_open_started` installs `ScopedLeastChangeAnswers`, which answers every OrcaSlicer dialog on the person's behalf and records it for the agent's load report. The Tips dialog has Yes and No, so it gets No.
- The launch resume (`ProjectAutosave` → `load_managed_checkpoint` → `load_files(vector, Restore)`) has no `FileOpenScope`, so the dialog reaches the person.

The sync setting itself is OrcaSlicer's `sync_after_load_file_show_flag`: when the key is absent the dialog is shown; when present, its value is used silently (`Plater.cpp` ~6901). It is stored only when "Don't show again" is ticked.

## What the agent already gets

The load report (`ToolResults.cpp` `load_report_result`) carries `loadFacts.selectedSetupChange.printerPreset {from, to}`, `setupPrinters` (the named printers with bed sizes), each object's `fitsSelectedBed` / `fitsSetupPrinters`, `fileFacts` (the printer and nozzle the 3MF says it was made for) and the answered dialogs. The `file-loaded` skill tells the model: when `selectedSetupChange.printerPreset` exists, name both selections and ask which printer the person intends; do not offer to print until that is resolved. That is the message of frame 1C-02, about fifteen seconds in. `printer_setup` then switches to a named printer; OrcaSlicer replaces the incompatible P1S process and filament presets with compatible A1 mini ones at that point (frame 2B-02's rows).

## Options

All four can be built in fork-owned files only. For reference, upstream churn over the last twelve months: `Plater.cpp` 568 commits, `PresetBundle.cpp` 157 (5 touching `load_config_file_config`), `Preset.cpp` 240, `Tab.cpp` 432, `GLCanvas3D.cpp` 285, `PartPlate.cpp` 187. Any option that edits those files pays that every rebase; none below needs to.

### Option 1. Keep the person's printer; import only the file's process, filament and object settings

First second: chip stays "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2 · 0.4", the 180 mm bed stays, the arrow overhangs it and the print-issue pill lights up. Nothing says the file wanted a P1S.

How: after `file_load_finished`, re-select the named printer that was selected before the load. Done through OrcaSlicer's `Tab::select_preset`, which on a dirty preset shows the "Transfer or discard" dialog; inside the open scope JusPrin's own auto-answer prefers Cancel and the switch would be refused, so it needs its own dialog listener answering Discard, or the lower-level `select_preset_by_name` + `on_config_change` route `SetupOptionsLoader.cpp` already uses. OrcaSlicer lines: 0. Fork code: adapter + SetupCommands, plus tests.

What it cannot do: OrcaSlicer will not keep a P1S process or filament preset selected on an A1 mini (incompatible), so the designer's process and filament values are dropped the moment the printer goes back, exactly as the agent's later switch drops them today. Keeping them would mean a new fork mechanism that copies the file's differences-from-system onto the A1 mini presets, some of which (temperatures, speeds, retraction) are printer-specific and wrong to carry. Object-level settings (per-object modifiers, painting, colours, plates) survive because they live in the model.

Agent: the load report would show no printer change; `fileFacts` still says the file was made for a P1S, so the skill can mention it, but the "which printer" question loses its trigger and would need a new rule. Launch: unaffected (the resumed project already has the person's printer), so the two paths agree by construction, and the launch session only needs to silence the dialog. Compatibility: changes what a 3MF open means for every file, including Bambu-owner files that match the printer (no effect there) and multi-printer users who open a file for their other printer (now wrong).

### Option 2. Apply the file's printer and mark the chip "from the file" until a printer is confirmed

First second: chip reads "Bambu Lab P1S · 0.4" with a warning tone and a second line or suffix "from the file · not one of your printers"; the P1S bed is drawn, as OrcaSlicer draws it. The chip's menu opens on the named printers that fit, with the file's printer as the first row, so one click resolves it. The setup card gets the same line.

How: no new state. The rule "the selected printer preset is not a named printer" (`Printers::is_named_printer`) already means "not one of yours"; `current_printer` gains a flag, `StatusRow::refresh_chip` and `PrinterMenu::show_root` draw it, the chip already has `StatusTone::Warning`. Cleared the instant the person or the agent selects a named printer, through the same refresh that follows any preset change. OrcaSlicer lines: 0. Fork code: `SetupCommands`, `StatusRow`, `PrinterMenu`, `PrinterFilamentChip`, the setup card in the page, plus a header snapshot test.

Agent: unchanged. The existing report and skill produce 1C-02; `printer_setup` clears the mark. Launch: the resumed project opens in the same marked state once the launch session stops the Tips dialog (see Coordination), so both paths look identical. Compatibility: 3MF loading unchanged; a person who really owns a P1S sees the mark until they add it as a printer, which is what the agent's "I have a P1S" button does.

### Option 3. Apply the file's printer and draw the mismatch on the plate as well as the chip

Option 2 plus: the person's own printer bed (the selected named printer before the load, 180 × 180) drawn as an outline over the P1S plate, so the arrow visibly crosses it, with the chip's menu offering that printer. This is the product definition's "compact pointer and any mismatch" taken literally.

How: the fork already owns an ImGui overlay hook on the canvas (`CanvasPresentationController::set_extra_overlay`, used by the print-issue overlay). The outline is the four bed corners projected through the camera and drawn as a 2D polyline, so no OrcaSlicer rendering line changes. It is drawn over the scene, not depth-tested, and needs the "printer before the load" remembered somewhere (the adapter has `m_setup_before_loads` for the report; the overlay would need it to persist with the project or be recomputed from the named printers). OrcaSlicer lines: 0. Fork code: Option 2 plus an overlay class and its layout tests, roughly twice the work.

Agent and launch: as Option 2. Risk: a second rectangle on the plate reads as a second plate to a new person; with several named printers the "which outline" choice is itself a decision.

### Option 4. Apply the file's printer and ask at once, without waiting for the model

Option 2 plus: the app itself (C++ host, from the load report's `setupPrinters` and `fitsSetupPrinters`, no model call) posts a card in the chat within the first second: "This file was saved for a Bambu Lab P1S, which isn't set up here. Print it on: [Bambu Lab A1] [Qidi X-Plus 4] [I have a P1S]". The agent's message fifteen seconds later elaborates; a button press runs `printer_setup`.

How: the host already draws the "Notes about this file" card from the report when no agent is set up; this is a sibling card drawn in both cases. OrcaSlicer lines: 0. Fork code: Option 2 plus a card in the page and a host rule for when it appears (only when the file's printer is not a named printer). Agent: the skill's question becomes redundant; either leave it or tell the skill the card exists. Launch: same as Option 2. Risk: two voices asking one question, in different words, a few seconds apart.

## Coordination with the launch-dialog task

Whichever option is chosen, launch and open must land in the same header state. Today they differ only because of the dialog, so the launch side needs one of:

- run the resume load under the same answer scope the open path uses (fork-only, mirrors `file_open_started`); or
- set OrcaSlicer's own `sync_after_load_file_show_flag` to `false` at startup, next to where the shell already sets `project_load_behaviour` (`ShellController.cpp` ~1629). Zero OrcaSlicer lines, and it also makes the open path deterministic instead of relying on the auto-answer.

The "Transfer or discard" dialog of frame 1 only appears after answering Yes, so it goes with the Tips dialog. Options 2 to 4 need nothing else from the launch side; Option 1 would need the launch side to also re-select the person's printer for a resumed project saved before the change. I have left a short note in the shared session folder for the launch session.

## Recommendation

Option 2, with Option 4's card as a follow-up if the fifteen-second wait still reads as too long after the chip is marked. Reasons: it is the only option that changes nothing about what a 3MF load means (designers' settings kept, OrcaSlicer's loading untouched, multi-printer owners unaffected), it needs no new state and no OrcaSlicer line, it is what the product definition asks the header to do, and the agent's report, skill and `printer_setup` already finish the job. Option 1 throws away the file's P1S settings and still cannot keep them for the A1 mini, so it trades a visible wrong printer for an invisible wrong setup. Option 3 is Option 2 plus a drawing that can be added later if the chip alone proves too quiet.

Decision needed from Kenneth: which option, and whether the launch side takes the `sync_after_load_file_show_flag` route or the answer-scope route (I lean to the flag).

On 2026-10-26 Kenneth decided the Agent pane's setup card takes a two-part shape, after a brainstorm from the reproduction in `card-headline-repro/` (jusprin-newui 889d28681c). The note is untracked at `setup-card-opening-message-design-note.md` in the main checkout (keep it untracked; see [[temp-docs-stay-untracked-and-visible]]).

The shape: above a rule, the person's purpose and the agent's plan headline, present only when someone wrote them (no preset name, project name or hint line stands in). Below the rule, OrcaSlicer facts: process · filament (+n) · "N settings changed" with All settings beside it, then estimates. A warning appears only as an annotation of the fact line it contradicts, one per line ("Printer last reported PLA" under the filament line, "Previous estimates · not current", "Plan needs another look · <reason>" under the plan from the app's existing mark). Print issues, nozzle and printer-model mismatches leave the card (canvas, chat, header chip). Moment-of-change notes (Updated, last step + Undo, estimate delta, edited-by-you, "Confirmed") leave the card for the timeline rows. The agent clears the plan's mark by re-recording or confirming; nothing is cleared automatically.

**Why:** Kenneth's test is "so simple there are obviously no problems": today's card has twelve named states from edge-case tweaks, and the card's reason to exist is to be the one place that is always *now*. He wants the mental model "agent's words above the line, facts below it", and warnings capped structurally so they cannot grow again.

**How to apply:** when implementing, do not reintroduce card-wide state labels or free-standing warning rows; a new warning must name the card line it annotates.
