## Writing UI code

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude
   artifacts are the source of truth (Kenneth, 2026-10-20; Figma is
   retired): the Design System
   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2"
   canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). The canvas
   frozen on 2026-10-27 (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v)
   is history, not a source. Change the token file to match, or, when the
   code's value is the one to keep, change the artifact first. Do not trust
   old commit messages about either.
6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
   not that the result looks right.
7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.

# Figma mirror: tools and backups > **2026-10-20: Figma is retired and out of date.** The two Claude artifacts are now the up-to-date JusPrin > design. Do NOT re-sync them from Figma: that would overwrite newer design work. Edit them directly: > copy the live files into `work/` (or read them with the Artifact tool), change them, publish only the changed > files, then rsync `work/` into `published/`. Remember the canvas keeps its own copy of the design system in > `project/ds/jusprin/` (tokens and component styles): change both artifacts together. `tools/composer/` holds > the scripts used since then (`render.py` screenshots boards with headless Chrome; `resize_board.py` fixes a > board's height in its file and in `canvas.json`; `build_filament_step.py` draws the Add-a-printer step-3 boards and their spec files, `measure_sheets.py` measures their sheet heights with headless Chrome). Before publishing to either artifact, do a plain `read` of its url: a publish after only `path` reads is refused as "haven't viewed the latest version". The Figma re-sync steps below are kept as history. This folder keeps what is needed to re-sync two Claude artifacts with the Figma file "JusPrin v2" (file key `jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH`), and to prove a re-sync breaks nothing. - Canvas "JusPrin v2": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v - JusPrin Design System: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL It lives outside the JusPrin repo on purpose: it is not product code, and untracked files in the repo mean "unfinished work" there. ## What is here - `published/` — an exact copy of what is published now (`canvas/project`, `ds/project`). Every re-sync is compared against it, then it is replaced by the new build. - `figma/spec3/.txt` — the Figma pages as last read (one text line per layer). `figma/vars.json` — Figma's variables, text styles and shadows as last read. - `tools/` — the scripts (below). - `visual/figma/*.png` — Figma's own screenshot of each page, used to score the artboards. `visual/scores-*.json` — the scores before and after the 2026-10-13 re-import. - `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` — the published files, the Figma reads and the scripts as they were before the re-import of 2026-10-13. Running those scripts on those reads reproduces those files byte for byte. ## Re-sync, step by step 1. Read Figma. For each page id (`0:1 1423:396 320:1053 160:59 9:153 359:116 1148:1287 1258:396 1328:2780`) call the Figma tool `use_figma` with the text of `tools/spec3_min.js`, replacing `__PAGE__` and `__OFFSET__` (0, then 20200, 40400, ... while the offset is below the returned `total`). About 35 calls; have background agents make them, because each reply is large. Run `tools/vars.js` once the same way and save its result as `figma/vars.json`. The script source is `tools/figma_spec3.js`; `python3 tools/minify.py tools/figma_spec3.js tools/spec3_min.js` rebuilds the one-line version. 2. Decode the replies from the session transcripts: `SESSION= OUT=figma python3 tools/collect.py` 3. Build into a scratch folder `new/`: export FIGMA_DIR=$PWD/figma DS_DIR=$PWD/new/ds REPO=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin rm -rf new && mkdir new && cp -R published/ds new/ds python3 tools/build_variants.py $REPO new/ds python3 tools/build_canvas.py $REPO new/canvas mkdir -p new/specs/project/screens && cp published/ds/project/tokens.json new/specs/project/ python3 tools/specs.py $REPO figma/spec3 new/specs/project/screens 4. Compare with what is published: `python3 tools/compare_builds.py published new`. With no change in Figma and no change in the scripts, every line must say "identical". Explain every file that is not before publishing. 5. Compare with Figma itself: take a screenshot of each Figma page (`get_screenshot`, maxDimension 8000) into `visual/figma/`, then `tools/visual_pages.py`, screenshot each `composite-.html` at full page size, and `tools/visual_compare.py`. No artboard may score worse than in `visual/scores-after.json`. 6. Publish only the changed files to the same artifact URLs, check the live pages, then replace `published/`. ## Known limits Photographs and 3D renders are flat placeholders. Artwork over 64px is not drawn. The page Figma marks obsolete is not read. Radial and image fills are placeholders (linear gradients are drawn). **Mechanism (verified in a scratch copy of the built app):** `PresetBundle::load_config_file_config` → `load_external_preset(... LoadAndSelect::Always)` finds the real P1S **system** preset by `printer_settings_id`, applies the file's values as a dirty edit, selects it and sets it visible (log: `select_preset: machine set Bambu Lab P1S 0.4 nozzle, idx 58 to visible`), then `reset_size 180→256`. It is not a project-embedded preset and never becomes a named printer. The chip shows `printer_model` for a non-named preset (`SetupCommands::current_printer`).

**Why launch and open differ:** every person-initiated open runs inside the fork's `FileOpenScope` (Plater.cpp 12145/14216) whose `ScopedLeastChangeAnswers` answers OrcaSlicer's "sync the printer information?" TipsDialog **No** unseen (it lands in the agent's load report / Notes card). The launch resume (`ProjectAutosave` → `load_managed_checkpoint` → `load_files(Restore)`) has no scope, so the dialog is a modal; Yes → `Tab::select_preset` on the dirty preset → "Transfer or discard". The dialog is gated by OrcaSlicer's app-config key `sync_after_load_file_show_flag` (absent → ask; present → used silently). Setting it `false` at startup beside `project_load_behaviour` (ShellController.cpp ~1629) removes it on both paths, zero Orca lines. The launch-dialog session (local_fb084e8c) owns that half.

**Decision (Kenneth, 2026-10-28): Option 2.** OrcaSlicer's load stays as is (designers' settings kept, 3MF loading unchanged). The chip is marked while `!Printers::is_named_printer(edited printer preset)`: triangle-alert 14 px in status.warning where the printer glyph was, "Bambu Lab P1S · 0.4 · from the file" (words in text.primary, like setup-card line annotations), tooltip with the file name. The chip's menu: first row "Bambu Lab P1S" + warning detail "From the file · not one of your printers" (no state word, no monitor); Nozzle, Plate; "YOUR PRINTERS" (instead of OTHER PRINTERS) with each printer's bed size as a second line (new); Printer settings…, Calibrate…, "Add a printer…" with the file's printer as meta. Mark clears when a named printer is selected (menu or agent `printer_setup`). The setup card gets no printer line (design-system rule: printer-model mismatches belong to the chip). The design for Option 2 is on the JusPrin v2 canvas, on a new page "File for another printer · header" (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ, version 1793200882-5346). The four renders are attached above. Nothing is implemented yet.

**What the boards show**

- Board 1, the header one second after the open, light and dark. The printer half reads "⚠ Bambu Lab P1S · 0.4 · from the file": the triangle-alert glyph in the warning colour takes the printer glyph's place, and the words are in the normal text colour, the same way the setup card annotates a line. The filament half is as OrcaSlicer loaded it, the file's three PLA colours. No dialog, and the same chip at launch when a resumed project carries a printer that is not one of yours.
- Board 2, the printer half state by state: a named printer as today, from the file, hover, menu open, keyboard focus, the tooltip with the file's name, and the alternative I do not recommend, the glyph alone with the words only in the tooltip and menu.
- Board 3, the chip's menu while marked. The first row names the file's printer with the reason "From the file · not one of your printers" and no state word, since no machine stands behind it. Nozzle and Plate are the stock rows. YOUR PRINTERS lists the six named printers in Home's order, each with its bed size under its name, so the 233 mm arrow can be sent to a bed that holds it without asking. The bed size is the one new thing on those rows. Add a printer… shows "Bambu Lab P1S" as its meta while the chip is marked.
- Board 4, after a choice: the chip is the named printer again, unmarked, or the P1S as a named printer once added.

**Two rules the boards follow**

- The mark is a rule, not stored state: it shows while the selected printer profile is not one of your named printers, and goes the moment one is selected, from the menu or by the agent.
- The setup card carries no printer line, because the design system assigns printer-model mismatches to the chip.

Also recorded: the publish and builder in the figma-mirror README, the decision in the options note and in the shared session notes for the launch-dialog session, and a memory note.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/local-agent-mode-sessions/skills-plugin/68a648b0-98a4-49c7-902b-ff471f8d1d46/7911d73c-5552-4877-a943-6a0eba3d7c4d/skills/built-in-browser

# Built-in browser

The built-in browser is a real browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, separate from the person's Chrome. Its tools are named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*` when the session itself runs inside the desktop app, and `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when the session runs in the cloud (started from the web, a phone, or the desktop app) and is linked to the person's computer. The names after the prefix are the same either way, Claude uses whichever prefix is actually present, and this skill refers to the tools by the part after the prefix.

If the only built-in browser tool present is `enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser`, Claude calls it first: it turns the built-in browser on for this conversation, and the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` tools appear once it has run.

## What the person can see

The browser pane shares the desktop app's side panel with artifacts, documents, and file previews, and the panel shows one of them at a time. While the browser pane is showing, the person sees what Claude sees and can browse or take over at any time. While something else is open in the panel, or the panel is closed, the built-in browser keeps working but the person cannot see it.

Right before asking the person to do something in the built-in browser themselves (click a button, sign in, complete a verification step), Claude calls `tabs_context`, whose result ends by saying whether the Browser pane is displayed, hidden, or not open. If the pane is not open, Claude opens the page first and checks again. If the pane is hidden, Claude first asks the person to bring the browser back in the Claude desktop app: press Cmd+Shift+B on Mac or Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows, or close whatever else is open in the side panel and click the globe icon (the Browser button). Claude then says what to do in the browser. Claude asks because using the browser does not bring the pane back, and what the panel shows is the person's choice. Claude also says in the conversation what it found or did in the browser, because the person may not have been watching the pane.

## Sign-ins persist, and they are the person's

The built-in browser keeps its own persistent profile, shared across the desktop app's sessions. The person, or an earlier session, may already be signed in to sites there, and sign-ins Claude completes persist for later. Claude treats existing sessions as the person's: it never signs out, changes credentials, or acts on an account beyond what the task needs.

## Tabs

The built-in browser has tabs. `preview_start` with a `url` opens an additional tab at that URL in one call and returns a `tabId`, leaving existing tabs untouched, so Claude prefers it over `tabs_create` followed by `navigate` when the destination is already known. `navigate`, `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, `computer`, `form_input`, and the console and network readers act on the tab named by `tabId`; omitting `tabId` targets the active tab, and `tabs_context` lists the open tabs.

## Loading via ToolSearch

Claude loads the built-in browser tools in bulk, not one-by-one: if they are in the deferred list, Claude loads them all in a single ToolSearch call whose query is their full name prefix, for example `{ query: "mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__", max_results: 64 }`.

## Reading pages

Claude prefers `get_page_text` and `read_page` over screenshots for reading, because they return the page's actual text and structure rather than pixels of the visible viewport. `computer` with action "screenshot" is for when the visual layout is the point or the person asks to see the page.

## Site approvals, blocked sites, and request_access

Depending on the person's approval settings, the person may be asked to approve a site before Claude acts on it, and some sites are blocked outright. Claude waits for a pending approval rather than working around it. If a page is refused or an approval is declined, Claude tells the person and moves on rather than retrying.

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, approvals can be answered from any of the person's devices and may take a moment to arrive, and the session may also have a `request_access` tool. If a browser tool answers that the site is not allowed yet and `request_access` is present, Claude calls it with that site's URL and scope "once" (or "site" when the task will keep using that site), waits for the person's answer, and then retries the original tool. Without `request_access`, a refused site is handled as above: Claude tells the person and moves on.

## What the built-in browser cannot open

The built-in browser cannot open `file://` URLs or `localhost` servers that Claude starts itself, because those run where Claude's shell runs, which is not where the browser pane runs. To show the person HTML that Claude generated, Claude uses an artifact instead.

## When the built-in browser cannot be reached

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, the pane runs in the Claude desktop app on the person's computer while Claude runs elsewhere, so it is reachable only while that app is open and online. If those tool calls cannot reach the desktop app (connection errors or no response), Claude tells the person the built-in browser looks offline on their computer rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

previously we have this rule:

<pasted_content id="1f42">
The rule was meant to keep warnings off the chip: the chip states facts and problems belong in the chat. It was never about whether the chip may show printer state, so my options note overstates it when it says option C (the chip showing “Sending…”, then the printer’s state) reverses a rule.
Where the wording comes from. The sentence first appears in commit 67361926b0 (2026-09-06, “Replace the header printer chip with a printer and spool chip”). It’s in two code comments, one on the printer menu’s first row in `PrinterMenu.cpp` and one on the chip’s tooltip. Neither the commit message nor `agent-docs/` says why. Entire couldn’t help either: this repository isn’t mirrored there, so it found neither the search text nor the commit’s checkpoint. The reasons are in a local Claude session transcript from the day before the commit (session `a140018b`, 6–7 September).
Kenneth’s own words. On 6 September, when the old design turned the chip red on a mismatch, he said: “Forget about chat warning. I think it’s actually very confusing if the chat actually influences the printer selection. It’s good enough for the chats to highlight that within the chat panel.”
What the design turned that into. The agent’s write-up (turn 15) said: “The chip never turns red or yellow. It states facts. The chat handles problems.” It also listed the change as a departure from earlier turns: a mismatch of plate, nozzle or filament against what the printer reports becomes a red line in the chat and on the pinned card. The red chip was dropped.
The supporting argument. Kenneth asked whether Bambu users expect mismatch warnings on the chip. The answer, which he accepted, was mostly no: Bambu Studio warns in the send dialog and on the printer itself, not where it shows what is loaded.
Where printer state was put. The design brief written that day split the content in two:

* The chip shows the printer name, nozzle, and the spool’s colour and name.
* The printer menu shows the printer’s name and its state: idle, printing, offline or not connected.
</pasted_content id="1f42">

it's documented. But I think this warning is warranted, although I can't exactly articulate why. Can you help me articulate what the correct rule should be? If necessary, go back to the history to review where that rule came from in the rationale behind it.

I have the trail now: the 6 September session, the commit comments, and the 26 October setup-card text. Here is what the history actually says, and the rule I'd write from it.

**Where the old rule came from.** On 6 September you were reacting to a design in which the chip turned red when the plan's plate, nozzle or filament disagreed with what the *connected printer reported*, and the chat drove that. Your words: "it's actually very confusing if the chat actually influences the printer selection." The write-up turned that into "The chip never turns red or yellow. It states facts. The chat handles problems," and the code comments say the same thing more precisely: "the chip makes no claim about the machine." The supporting argument was that Bambu owners expect loaded-material and nozzle warnings at send time and on the printer, not where the app shows what is loaded. So the rule had two real subjects: mismatches against the *physical machine*, and the *chat* steering what the chip shows. Neither is what the "from the file" mark is.

**Why the mark is warranted.** The chip's job is to say what the project will be sliced for. After opening that 3MF the plain answer, "Bambu Lab P1S · 0.4", is not a fact the person can use: it reads as one of their printers, and it isn't. The mark is not a warning placed on top of the chip's fact. It is the missing half of the fact. It comes from OrcaSlicer's own preset state (the selected profile is not a named printer), not from the chat and not from anything the machine reported, and nothing the chat says can create it or clear it. So it passes the old rule's two real tests while failing only the overstated one-liner.

**The rule I'd write:**

> The chip states the selection: the printer profile the project will be sliced for, its nozzle, the project's filaments. It may qualify that statement, and must, when the plain statement would mislead; the qualification is about the selection itself, comes from OrcaSlicer's own state, and holds regardless of what the chat says. The chip makes no claim about the physical machine: what is loaded, which plate is on, which nozzle is fitted, whether it is connected or busy. Those belong to the chat, the setup card's line annotations, the printer menu's first row, and the send dialog. The chat never changes the chip.

Four tests for any future mark:

1. Is it about the selection or about the machine? Machine means not on the chip.
2. Would the chip's plain text mislead without it? If not, it is a warning, and warnings go to the chat.
3. Does it come from OrcaSlicer's preset state, or from an observation or a judgement? Observations and judgements go to the chat.
4. Can the chat create or clear it? If yes, it is not the chip's.

Run through the cases: "from the file" passes all four. "Printer last reported PLA" fails test 1 and stays a card annotation. "Not connected" and "Printing" are machine state and stay in the menu row. A project that selects the person's own P1S while their A1 mini is the connected one is a legitimate selection, so the chip stays plain and the send dialog handles it.

**One correction this implies.** The 26 October setup-card text in the design-system doc says "nozzle and printer-model mismatches [belong] to the header's printer and filament chip." That was written to keep warnings off the card and assigned them to the chip without checking the chip's rule. Under the rule above, only the selection mark is the chip's; nozzle and model mismatches against the connected machine belong to the chat and the send dialog. That sentence should change.

On the "Sending…" question in your note: the September brief put printer state in the menu, not on the chip, as a layout decision, not as part of the warning rule. Under the rule above a job's progress is neither selection nor machine state, so it is not the chip's either.

Its printer half is marked while the selected printer profile is not one of the person's named printers and not OrcaSlicer's placeholder (`Printers::printer_from_file`), which is what opening a 3MF saved for another printer leaves selected: the 14 DIP `triangle-alert` glyph in `status.warning` takes the printer glyph's place, the label reads "<model> · <nozzle> · from the file" in `text.primary`, and the tooltip names the file. The chip's menu then opens with that printer and the Body Small line "From the file · not one of your printers", a row that cannot be pressed; every other row is the stock menu. Nothing is stored: the mark goes when a named printer is selected, from the menu or by the agent. Decided 2026-10-28; boards 1 to 5 of "File for another printer" on the canvas's Printer & Material Settings page.

python3 - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md'); s = p.read_text()
old1 = "print issues belong to the canvas and the chat, nozzle and printer-model mismatches to the header's printer and filament chip."
new1 = "print issues belong to the canvas and the chat; a mismatch between the selection and the connected machine (its nozzle, its model, what it has loaded) belongs to the chat and to the send dialog, never to the chip (see Header chip)."
assert old1 in s; s = s.replace(old1, new1)
old2 = "- Header chip: 28 DIP high, `chip` radius (`component.chip`). Its printer half is marked while"
new2 = """- Header chip: 28 DIP high, `chip` radius (`component.chip`). The chip states the selection: the printer profile the project will be sliced for, its nozzle, the project's filaments. It may qualify that statement, and must, when the plain statement would mislead; the qualification is about the selection itself, comes from OrcaSlicer's own state, and holds regardless of what the chat says. The chip makes no claim about the physical machine: what is loaded, which plate is on, which nozzle is fitted, whether it is connected or busy. Those belong to the chat, the setup card's line annotations, the printer menu's first row, and the send dialog. The chat never changes the chip. (Kenneth, 2026-09-06, restated 2026-10-28: the September rule "the chip states facts and never warns" was about the chat steering the chip and about mismatches with the connected machine; it was not about the selection.) Four tests for any mark proposed for the chip:
  1. Is it about the selection or about the machine? Machine means not on the chip.
  2. Would the chip's plain text mislead without it? If not, it is a warning, and warnings go to the chat.
  3. Does it come from OrcaSlicer's preset state, or from an observation or a judgement? Observations and judgements go to the chat.
  4. Can the chat create or clear it? If yes, it is not the chip's.

  The one mark in use passes all four. Its printer half is marked while"""
assert old2 in s; s = s.replace(old2, new2)
p.write_text(s); print('written')
EOF
